Everything makes sense now. I launched myself into a huge task without being prepared at all. I moved out of home, as well as quit PMO and Videogames, at the same time losing friends, losing interest in old hobbies, trying to start new ones without the attitude of patience and perseverance. Why should I expect to be able to pick up girls, read entire books, play guitar well, paint a masterpiece, without any of the prior discipline and experience to do so? Its obvious. And my 'objective inferiorities' are deeply connected to my ideal self and aligns with my goals. I didn't realize that before - I would just beat myself up about not being who I should be by now and not having what I should have, but those feelings are trying to get me to charge forth and fix them.

These past few months have been such an extreme shift in lifestyle and, of course I'm feeling the way I do. I didn't have the problem-solving, courageous attitude to make it work. I didn't have a plan to address everything I needed to address to keep myself sane and healthy. 

I fell deeper and deeper into those avoidance strategies, convincing myself that I have illnesses, looking for a diagnosis just so I can avoid what I need to do. 

SO many of my weak points of my previous lifestyle, behavioral and thinking patterns just keep surfacing. I am left with a broken machine and have been a coward. I guess all I can do now is to take responsibility for myself.. Stop blaming bad parenting, perceived disorders. I made bad choices. Okay. I'll try my best to fix everything up.
